# 1. Architecture file grammar

Date: 2026-10-31 · Status: accepted

## Context

The architecture file (`<name>.arch.md`) is the format the rest of the system depends on. The agent reads it to write code; people read and diff it; v2 regeneration will diff two versions of it. It is derived from the board file by `serialize()` and never hand-edited.

## Decision

An indentation-based, line-oriented pseudocode, two spaces per level:

```
# architecture: <board name>
# generated by scaffold; edit the board, not this file

module <name>  @id <id>
  fn <name><signature or ()>  @id <id>
    intent: <one sentence>
    steps:
      - <step>
  module <name>  @id <id>
    ...
```

- **Containment is indentation.** A block's children sit one level deeper than it.
- **Every block line ends with `@id <id>`**, two spaces after the content. Agent errors cite these IDs.
- **Order is deterministic:** among siblings, sort by kind order (`function`, then `module`), then name, then id. Positions, sizes and array order never affect output.
- **Top-level blocks are separated by one blank line**; nested blocks are not.
- Block properties (`intent:`, `steps:`) sit one level under their block line. Empty steps are omitted. An empty signature renders as `()`.
- The file ends with a single newline.

Later tickets add block kinds, edges and notes by extending this grammar: new kinds get a keyword and a slot in the kind order; edges and notes get property lines. Existing lines never change shape.

## Consequences

- Moving blocks around never produces a diff; renaming does.
- The golden files in `test/fixtures/` are the executable form of this ADR.
- Signatures are free text, so the grammar is not machine-parseable below the block line. That is intentional: the reader is an LLM, and the board file is the machine format.
